rulings.challenge_claim: The opening seam is carried by the English rendering of the row's onset verse, whose pointed bytes supply neither a vocative nor an imperative shape, while the row's 2 Hebrew splices both fall inside the unit rather than at either edge.
rulings.grounds: The core defect is real and byte-grounded, and two framings are wrong. REAL: the row's opening seam carries no Hebrew at all, and the onset bytes הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.8) show no vocative and no second-person form, so the row's 'fresh addressee' rests on the rendering -- a miss against the standing rule that pointed splices with tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, and it falls on the row's own primary ground. WRONG (i): 'both fall inside the unit rather than at either edge' is byte-false -- oshb:Isa.43.13 is the span's TERMINAL verse and the row cites גַּם מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא (byte tier) precisely as the unit's close, so only the OPENING edge is Hebrew-unsupported. WRONG (ii): the self-identification run does not bracket 'this very span'. Byte tier puts כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא at MT 43:10 and גַּם מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא at MT 43:13 (sweep: 3 MT verses book-wide at byte tier -- MT 43:10, MT 43:13, MT 46:4; 5 verses at accent-stripped tier), and MT 43:10 is the span's SECOND verse, so the pair brackets MT 43:10-43:13, not the row's MT 43:8-43:13; if anything it argues a rival onset at MT 43:10 rather than corroborating the row's own seam. What does stand at the seam in the bytes, unused by both the row and the challenge, is a participant change: MT 43:7 closes a first-person divine clause addressed to 'you', while הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר opens a directive concerning a third party and כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.9) summons the nations -- explicit in the bytes and therefore tier-1 available. OL's remaining objects verify exactly: the postpositive utterance signature stands at MT 43:10 and MT 43:12, וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.12), 2 verses in MT chs 42-45 and 23 book-wide at skeleton tier; and the in-span mark set is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 43:10 and MT 43:13, tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-002. Field boundary_rationale: add a byte-tier pointed splice at the row's OWN opening seam -- הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר at oshb:Isa.43.8 and the nations-summons כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ at oshb:Isa.43.9 -- and restate the seam signal as the byte-visible participant change (first-person divine speech to 'you' at MT 43:7 giving way to a directive concerning a third party plus the nations-summons at MT 43:8-43:9). Do NOT assert an imperative or a vocative at MT 43:8: no per-token parsing layer is staged and the bytes carry neither; if a directive force is claimed, state it as a functional reading. Optional, not required: keep the self-identification pair as an internal cohesion note with its true reach named (MT 43:10 and MT 43:13, byte tier, 3 MT verses book-wide) -- never as an inclusio over the span. Field boundary_evidence_refs: mirror any newly argued verse. Test the cure must pass: every added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier against the ref it is cited under, and the seam claim must name a signal present in the bytes of the verses on either side of the seam -- the test that killed the original was that the row's own onset verse carried zero Hebrew.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's repeated form-class label is contradicted by the pointed bytes it rests on, and the participle chain it argues from is spliced at 1 of its 2 members.
rulings.grounds: Both halves byte-verified. MT 43:18 reads אַֽל תִּזְכְּר֖וּ and אַל תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.18) -- the negative particle plus a prefix-conjugation form, the prohibitive pattern, which is not the imperative form the row's prose names three times across boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes; and the verse the row pairs with it opens הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.19), a presentative plus participle that is not directive at all. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims carrying digit-grade discipline, and no per-token parsing layer is staged, so the honest options are the byte-visible pattern or a stated functional reading -- the row gives neither. The participle point also verifies: the row splices כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.16) but argues a two-member chain whose second member, הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב וָס֖וּס (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.17), is what makes it a chain and is argued in prose with no form and no splice. Severity low is correct: the bounds are not in question -- the onset frame at MT 43:16 is byte-verified as the divine class, not the royal-messenger class that stands only at MT 36:4, MT 36:14, MT 36:16 and MT 37:3 -- and the in-span SAMEKH at MT 43:21 (tier-3, single-witness) is disclosed, so both items are prose-accuracy and splice-completeness, additively curable with no boundary consequence.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-004. ONE edit across three fields (boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, device_notes), since the rival sentence rests on the same label: replace every 'imperative' form-label for MT 43:18-43:19 with either the byte-visible pattern (negation plus prefix conjugation, i.e. prohibitive, at MT 43:18; presentative plus participle at MT 43:19) or an explicitly-stated functional reading such as 'directive in force'. Field boundary_rationale additionally: splice הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב וָס֖וּס at oshb:Isa.43.17 at byte tier so both members of the participle chain the row argues are spliced, and add oshb:Isa.43.17 to boundary_evidence_refs if the ref layer requires it. Test the cure must pass: every form-class word in the row re-checks against the pointed bytes at its cited ref -- the test that killed the original was that 'imperative' does not describe the negative particle plus prefix conjugation at MT 43:18 -- and the added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with the normalization dry-run clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: The contrast the row uses to justify its opening seam is byte-false at the seam itself, and the signal that is byte-visible there -- a shift from plural to singular address -- goes unnamed.
rulings.grounds: A defect is real but narrower than charged, and the replacement signal proposed is weaker than the one actually at the seam. REAL: the seam-adjacent bytes are first-person divine speech, עַם זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.21), so the row's word 'self-predication' misnames the seam -- the third person at MT 43:20-43:21 is reference to the animals and to the people, not divine self-description. NOT byte-false, however: the row predicates third-person self-predication of the preceding ORACLE, and that unit does open on a participial self-predication under its messenger frame, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ followed by הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב וָס֖וּס (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.16 and oshb:Isa.43.17) -- byte-true as a unit-level statement, defective only in seam-adjacency. And the strongest byte-visible seam signal is not the number shift proposed: the plural forms cited, הֲל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּהָ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.19) and the MT 43:18 prohibitives, sit three and four verses back from the seam -- the same distance defect the challenge charges the row with -- while the seam itself turns from third-person reference at MT 43:21 to direct singular address, וְלֹא אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.22), which is what the row's own opening clause names and splices. Two sub-points do not survive as defects. The doubled-pronoun evidence, אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י at MT 43:11 against אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י ה֛וּא at MT 43:25 -- verified identical at ACCENT-STRIPPED tier only, byte tier isolating each to its own verse, 2 verses in MT chs 42-45 -- cannot be demanded of strongest_rejected_alternative, which the field contract caps at one sentence, and the row already argues MT 43:25 in device_notes. The in-span mark set is disclosed complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 43:24 and MT 43:28, tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-005. Field boundary_rationale: replace the clause naming the preceding oracle's third-person self-predication with the seam-adjacent contrast, splicing BOTH sides at byte tier -- third-person reference to the people at oshb:Isa.43.21, עַם זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ, against the direct singular address already spliced at oshb:Isa.43.22, וְלֹא אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב. Do NOT recast the driver as a plural-to-singular number shift: those forms are three to four verses back from the seam. Optional strengthening, not required, field device_notes: add the doubled-pronoun pair at MT 43:11 and MT 43:25 with its tier named as ACCENT-STRIPPED (not byte) in support of holding the lawsuit whole. Test the cure must pass: every contrast term in the rationale must describe the bytes of the verses on either side of the seam it argues -- the test that killed the original was that 'self-predication' does not describe MT 43:21 -- and every added run re-collates at byte tier with its tier named.

rulings.challenge_claim: The divine-speech frame is attached to the wrong bytes: the clause the row labels the frame formula is the fear-not clause that follows it, and the frame itself sits one verse inside the row rather than at its onset.
rulings.grounds: The headline is byte-exact. MT 44:2 runs כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ and only then אַל תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.2), and the English witness sets the same order at web:Isa.44.2, so the clause the row labels the frame formula is the fear-not formula that the frame introduces. In a book where frame ownership is a flagged hazard -- 44 divine frames against exactly 4 royal-messenger sites at MT 36:4, MT 36:14, MT 36:16 and MT 37:3 -- a row that names the formula, points it at the wrong clause and never names whose frame it is, is a tier-1 misattribution rather than a wording slip. The second half also verifies: the span opens at MT 44:1, whose onset וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.1) is a defensible tier-1 imperative-plus-vocative onset, but the speech frame sits one verse inside the unit and the row nowhere discloses it -- the fact its own rival, which folds MT 44:1-44:5 back into the lawsuit, most needs answered. One tightening on the servant sub-point, which is not merely true of the two verses taken together: the servant noun attaches to Jacob in both verses and to Israel in neither -- וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ at MT 44:1 and וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ at MT 44:2 are chosen-clauses, and Jeshurun is not Israel -- while the outright naming of Israel as servant stands at יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.21). The row decides no referent, so the held classic is untouched. The echo claim is untiered as charged: וְעַתָּ֞ה at MT 43:1 against וְעַתָּ֥ה at MT 44:1 match at accent-stripped tier, not byte. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (PE at MT 44:5, tier-3, single-witness). Medium severity is right: a misattributed tier-1 formula plus an undisclosed frame position on a high-confidence row.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-006. Field boundary_rationale, four changes. (a) Re-attach the label: name כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier) as the divine-frame formula, with its frame owner stated as the divine class, and אַל תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (same ref, byte tier) as the fear-not formula it introduces. (b) Add one clause disclosing that the frame stands at MT 44:2, one verse inside the unit, and that the onset ground is the imperative plus vocative at MT 44:1. (c) Correct 'Jacob and Israel NAMED as servant here' to what the bytes carry -- Jacob named servant, with Israel at MT 44:1 and Jeshurun at MT 44:2 standing in the parallel chosen-clauses -- and keep the referent undecided. (d) Tier-label the MT 43:1 / MT 44:1 opening echo as ACCENT-STRIPPED, not byte, or splice both forms and name the tier. Test the cure must pass: every formula name in the row must sit on the bytes it labels at its cited ref, every speech frame claim must name whose frame it is, and every recurrence claim must carry its collated tier -- the test that killed the original was that the quoted English at web:Isa.44.2 is the fear-not clause and not the messenger formula.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's 2 Hebrew-dependent claims -- the closing rock epithet and the witness catchword across its own seam -- are each argued with 0 Hebrew splices, in two classes this book flags for byte discipline.
rulings.grounds: Verified: both Hebrew-dependent claims carry zero splices. The closing epithet is וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.8) and the row quotes only English for it; the rock / adversary / Tyre homograph family is a named hazard class (the contiguous skeleton stands in 23 verses book-wide across all three roles), so the claim owes both the form and the named object and the row supplies neither. The cross-seam witness catchword in device_notes is likewise unspliced and untiered: וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י at MT 44:8 against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ at MT 44:9 (byte tier at each ref) share the root and differ in every affix. One correction to the challenge's framing: 'catchword pull' does not assert identity, so the defect is the missing splice and tier label, not an overstated identity. The wider-chain digits verify exactly -- the second-person witness formula at MT 43:10, MT 43:12 and MT 44:8 (3 verses in MT chs 42-45, skeleton tier) and the third-person counter-witnesses יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ at MT 43:9 and MT 44:9 (the only 2 verses book-wide carrying that skeleton) -- but mapping the whole neighbourhood is an enhancement, not an obligation, so it does not raise the severity. NEW FINDING, missed by both primaries: the same device_notes sentence places the idol-makers' witnesses 'two verses later', when the row's own witness language stands at web:Isa.44.8 and the counter-witnesses at web:Isa.44.9 -- ONE verse later. Positional and distance words carry the same discipline as digits; web:Isa.44.9 is correctly mirrored in the row's refs, so only the distance word is wrong. Bounds stand: the onset frame at MT 44:6 is byte-verified divine, and the PE at MT 44:5 before the span with no mark inside it is the whole of what the tier-3 single-witness layer owes.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-007. (a) Field boundary_rationale: splice וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר at oshb:Isa.44.8 at byte tier for the closing epithet and NAME the object -- the rock epithet, distinguished from the adversary and the Tyre homographs on the same skeleton. (b) Field device_notes: splice both witness forms at byte tier, וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י at oshb:Isa.44.8 and וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ at oshb:Isa.44.9, and label the recurrence at its true level (shared root, differing affixes; not identity at any tier). (c) Field device_notes: correct 'two verses later' to one verse later. Test the cure must pass: every Hebrew-dependent claim in the row carries a byte-collated splice at its cited ref with its count-object named, every recurrence carries its tier, and every distance or position word re-derives from the cited refs -- the tests that killed the original were two Hebrew claims with zero splices in flagged homograph and catchword classes, and a distance word that does not survive re-derivation.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (high): the unit's opening boundary is argued from a register/person shift alone, with no koh-amar, hoy, massa or addressee-shift signal marking it -- which the row's own text concedes -- and its device notes separately cross-reference a neighbouring row's later field use. OL (medium): the register shift is unsupported in the pointed bytes and contradicted by the one staged layout witness, while the person shift is byte-true and sufficient on its own; the forming root that opens the row is the frame word of the units on both sides, a byte-true cross-seam pull left undisclosed; plus two disclosure items (the out-of-span ketiv/qere at MT 44:24, and undisclosed extraordinary points at MT 44:9).
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: partly the SAME defect, partly DISTINCT. Same on one item -- both flag the device_notes sentence that cites the ketiv/qere at oshb:Isa.44.24 'for the adjoining row's use of the same field'; LF's framing is the correct one, since a positional cross-row reference naming another row's field is barred outright by the register law and cross-row references are verse-anchored. DISTINCT on the decisive item: LF treats register and person shift as one invalid driver and puts the boundary itself in doubt at high severity, while OL splits them and holds the person shift byte-true and sufficient. My re-derivation splits with OL and against LF's severity. The register half fails exactly as OL says: the pointed extract carries no prose/poetry layer at all, and the only staged layout witness contradicts the label -- the English sets EVERY verse of Isa.44.9-Isa.44.20 in poetry lines (verified: 12 of 12 verses, 47 lines), tier-4 in either direction and incapable of carrying a boundary ground. The person half, however, is not a register class and is byte-true: MT 44:8 carries first-person divine speech with second-person plural addressees, הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.8), and MT 44:9 opens יֹֽצְרֵי פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.9) with speaker and addressee both gone -- across MT 44:9-44:20 every first-person form sits inside the idol-maker's quoted or reported speech (MT 44:16, MT 44:17, MT 44:19, and -- missing from OL's enumeration -- הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי at MT 44:20), with no divine first person anywhere in the span. The disappearance of both speaker and addressee is a participant/scene shift explicit in the bytes, which the evidence policy ranks tier-1; it is not a parallelism/register class. So LF's 'no tier-1 signal' does not survive and its high severity is not sustained: the seam is not evidentially empty, no boundary change is warranted, and what is defective is the row's LABEL for its own driver. The forming-root pull verifies exactly: יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י at MT 43:21, וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן at MT 44:2 and יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד לִי֙ at MT 44:21 (byte tier at each ref) frame the units on both sides, and the same root recurs inside the satire at יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל (MT 44:10) and יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ (MT 44:12) and in the row's own onset word -- sweep: 9 verses in MT chs 43-44 carry the contiguous forming skeleton, with the plene spelling attested 0 times in that window (skeleton tier; the Niphal at MT 43:10 correctly falls outside a contiguous-substring object). That device straddles this row's seams and argues continuity unless disclosed. Two disclosure items part company. The out-of-span ketiv/qere at MT 44:24 is a real defect, the one both primaries share. The extraordinary points are byte-true and rare exactly as OL says -- three upper-dot codepoints in וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ at MT 44:9, sweep 1 verse across 1,291 MT verses, single-witness, a letter-byte fact and not a seg, with no small- or large-letter claim implied -- but they are NOT a row defect: no staged inventory defines an extraordinary-points arm, the disclosure contract runs to the staged inventories, the dotted word lies outside the run the row actually splices, and instructing an author to manufacture a claim no inventory can validate is the wrong cure. Route it to the orchestrator as an inventory question. NEW FINDING: the register label is carried in a SECOND field neither primary named -- literature_type_guess also reads the unit as prose-register description inside surrounding poetry -- so the cure's field scope is wider than either packet states. Credit, so the author does not 'fix' what is right: the judgment_oracle value is compliant under the operative-category law with its one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes; and the in-span disclosure set is complete and correctly typed -- ketiv/qere at MT 44:17, SAMEKH at MT 44:20, and the small nun at MT 44:14 (verified as the ONE special-letter seg in the book, single-witness, with no position claim made).
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-008: ONE driver swap with its dependent fields; the span is NOT changed and no boundary proposal is made. (a) Delete the prose-inside-poetry register ground from boundary_rationale AND the matching clause from literature_type_guess. (b) In boundary_rationale, argue the opening seam from the byte-visible participant shift, splicing BOTH sides at byte tier -- הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י at oshb:Isa.44.8 against יֹֽצְרֵי פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ at oshb:Isa.44.9 -- and state that no divine first person stands anywhere in MT 44:9-44:20, the span's first-person forms all sitting inside the idol-maker's quoted or reported speech. (c) In observed_substrate_signals, swap the register-shift key for a participant/addressee-shift key in the dotted taxonomy; because a driver swap is a dependent-field trigger, re-open strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence in the SAME edit (unit_type judgment_oracle and its deviation disclosure re-derive unchanged from the bytes; the rival that keeps the satire inside the trial speech survives and must be restated without the conceded 'no addressee marker' wording, which the bytes now answer). (d) In device_notes, disclose the forming-root chain across the row's seams with its tier named (skeleton; 9 verses in MT chs 43-44; plene spelling 0 in that window). (e) Delete the device_notes sentence about the adjoining row's use of the field AND the oshb:Isa.44.24 ketiv/qere entry from boundary_evidence_refs together as ONE edit -- cross-row references are verse-anchored, and that note is already carried by the row that argues the verse. Do NOT add an extraordinary-points claim: that object has no staged inventory arm and is an orchestrator question, not author work. Test the cure must pass: the rationale carries no tier-4 layout class in a driver role, the seam ground is a byte-collated splice on BOTH sides of the seam, the row carries no cross-row or field reference, and the refs mirror still resolves every verse argued in prose -- the tests that killed the original were the row's own concession sentence and the layout witness that contradicts its register label.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row discloses 1 cross-seam tie, an untiered recurrence whose two forms match at no tier above the root, and its mark disclosure stops at the edge before the span while a petuchah -- the rarer of the layer's 2 mark types (41 PE against 168 SAMEKH over 209 marked MT verses) -- stands at the verse it argues as its closing boundary.
rulings.grounds: Both halves verify. (1) The redemption tie is asserted as a bare recurrence with no tier: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ at MT 44:22 against כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל at MT 44:23 (byte tier at each ref) are different conjugations of one root, not the same form at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier, so an unqualified 'recurs' overstates it -- the honest citation is a root-level catchword (the redemption skeleton stands in 6 verses of MT chs 42-45, verified exactly). Every recurrence claim is tier-labelled at write time, so this is a live rule, not taste. (2) The mark disclosure is asymmetric on exactly the question the row raises: the row cites the SAMEKH at MT 44:20, one verse before its span, and omits the PE at MT 44:23, one verse after it -- and the inventory verifies the challenge's framing (209 marked MT verses, 41 PE against 168 SAMEKH; the layer's section here runs MT 44:21-44:23, grouping the row's span with the very verse its disclosed rival wants to absorb). Span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry is unconditional and is the campaign's heaviest sweep, so engaging one edge and not the other is a defect even though the layer is tier-3 single-witness, absence is never counterevidence, and the cut itself stands. One sub-point in the challenge's evidence is an enhancement, not a defect, and the remedy must not treat it as mandatory: the backward blotting pair מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ at MT 43:25 against מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ at MT 44:22 (byte tier at each ref; the 2 verses in MT chs 42-45 carrying both roots) does not straddle THIS row's own seam -- two units intervene -- so the cross-seam cohesion rule does not reach it. The servant naming is byte-correct and the referent left undecided, as the challenge credits.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-009. (a) Field device_notes: tier-label the redemption tie honestly as a ROOT-level catchword between כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22) and כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23), splicing both at byte tier at their own refs and stating that the two forms are not identical at any tier. (b) Fields boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs: add the PE at MT 44:23 with its TYPE named (petuchah, never conflated with setumah), single-witness, tier-3, AND its direction -- that the layer's section runs MT 44:21-44:23 and therefore corroborates the disclosed rival rather than the cut, which rests on the tier-1 addressee turn. The absence of a mark at the row's own closing seam is not counterevidence and must not be written as support. Do the symmetry as a SWEEP over both span-relevant edges, not as a spot fix. The backward tie to MT 43:25 is optional enrichment only. Test the cure must pass: for the row's span, every mark at or adjacent to BOTH edges appears with its type, tier and witness disclosure, and every recurrence claim carries its collated tier -- the tests that killed the original were the untiered 'recurs' and the uncited PE on which the row's own rival depends.

rulings.challenge_claim: The isolation of Isa.44.23 as its own doxology row leaves a byte-true redeemer catchword undisclosed on BOTH of the row's seams, and its division-mark citation reaches only the rear seam while the same layer groups the three verses the disclosed rival joins.
rulings.grounds: Both defects verify. (1) The redeemer root runs through the row's front and rear seams in three consecutive verses and three inflections -- כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ at MT 44:22, כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל at MT 44:23, כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ at MT 44:24 (byte tier at each ref) -- and the challenge tiers it correctly as a root/skeleton chain and NOT a byte-identical refrain (sweep: 21 verses book-wide carry the contiguous redeemer skeleton, verified exactly; 6 verses in MT chs 42-45). The row argues its front seam from the addressee turn alone and its rear seam from the following frame, naming the lexical hook at neither, so a device straddling both seams of a ONE-verse row stands undisclosed against the row's own and only rival. The rear-seam link is the sharper half and is undisclosed across the whole neighbourhood, not merely here: the preceding row discloses only the front-seam tie, and does so in English without a tier. The name pair also recurs at MT 44:21 and MT 44:23 (Jacob's skeleton: 40 verses book-wide, 11 in MT chs 42-45 -- verified). (2) The mark citation carries no direction: the PE at MT 44:23 is listed in the evidence refs and never mentioned in prose, while the layer's section runs MT 44:21-44:23 (SAMEKH after MT 44:20, PE after MT 44:23), so the mark reaches only the far side of the row's closing seam and its grouping runs WITH the rival, not with the cut. The cut itself is not in doubt and I do not disturb it: the addressee turn is tier-1 and byte-visible -- direct singular address at MT 44:22 against the cosmic imperative summons רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם, הָרִ֨יעוּ֙ and פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.23) -- and the strategy names this verse among the doxology-closure units isolable by tier-1 signals. One precision on the challenge's own credit remark: of those three summons forms only רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם is verse-initial; the other two are clause-initial inside the verse, and position claims carry the same discipline everywhere.
rulings.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-010; the span is NOT changed. (a) Field device_notes: disclose the redeemer catchword on BOTH seams with its tier named -- a root/skeleton-level chain across כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22), כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23) and גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Isa.44.24), each spliced at byte tier at its own ref, stated explicitly as NOT a byte-identical refrain -- and say that it argues continuity which the tier-1 addressee turn overrides. (b) Field boundary_rationale: name the direction of the tier-3 mark -- petuchah after MT 44:23 (single-witness), which reaches the far side of the closing seam and groups MT 44:21-44:23 with the disclosed rival, so it is not support for isolating the verse; the cut rests on the addressee shift. (c) Field boundary_evidence_refs: mirror MT 44:24 if the catchword disclosure argues it. Test the cure must pass: every device straddling either seam of the span is disclosed with its collated tier, and every mark listed in the evidence refs is either argued in prose with its direction named or removed -- the tests that killed the original were an undisclosed cross-seam root chain and a direction-less mark citation.
